sources.entry: OpenQuack - Privacy-first voice dictation tool that transcribes locally with WhisperKit and inserts text at the cursor with a hotkey. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/larryxiao/openquack) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
OpenQuack - Local-only voice dictation for macOS — press a hotkey, speak, and the transcript is pasted at the cursor. Runs WhisperKit on Apple Silicon with no telemetry.
28. OpenQuack - On-device voice dictation for macOS — transcribes a 5-minute clip in 2.8 s; noise-robust, paste at cursor. 99 languages, ~8 MB, no telemetry. MIT.

summary.one_liner: OpenQuack is a menu-bar voice dictation app for macOS that transcribes speech locally with WhisperKit and pastes the text at the cursor when you press a hotkey.
summary.what_it_does: Press a hotkey (default ⌃⇧Space, or fn/Globe), speak, press again, and the transcript is inserted at the cursor in any app, with an option to fall back to the clipboard. Transcription runs on-device with Whisper via WhisperKit, and the README says no audio, text, or telemetry leaves the Mac by default. It supports 99 languages with auto-detect on by default, and applies smart formatting (capitalisation, punctuation, "um/uh" removal) plus a custom dictionary for proper nouns. An experimental, opt-in on-device LLM "polish" pass can tidy phrasing, and the editable prompt can be changed in Settings. Other features include auto-stop after silence and launch at login. Users can optionally point transcription at their own OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which is off by default.
use_cases: dictate text into any app on macOS
transcribe long voice memos quickly on a Mac
clean up speech transcripts with a local LLM
how_to_run: Or download the DMG and drag OpenQuack into Applications
First launch: right-click → Open → Open (one-time Gatekeeper bypass)
Grant Microphone permission when macOS asks
Pick a hotkey in Settings → Shortcut (default ⌃⇧Space)
notable: Streams Whisper transcription while you speak, so a 5-minute clip finishes about 3 seconds after you stop (README benchmark on baseline M4 / 16 GB)
Local-first by default, with no account, signup, or telemetry
Optional on-device LLM polish pass with an editable system prompt, off by default
Tiny footprint: about 8 MB app bundle and about 120 MB RAM while idle, per the README
Auto-stops recording and keeps what was said if the microphone changes mid-recording
caveats: First launch requires a manual Gatekeeper bypass (right-click → Open) when installed from the DMG
LLM polish is marked experimental and off by default
Remote transcription endpoint is optional and breaks the fully local default when enabled
Benchmark figures come from the README's own measurements and are not independently verified
keywords: transcribe voice to text on mac
